what_happened.line: The Open Space Committee voted to recommend the town not sell the tax liens on four parcels, so the town can try to acquire them for open space.
The committee accepted its chair's resignation and appointed a new chair; the vice chair stays on until May, when the position will be voted.
Members approved the draft annual report and two sets of earlier minutes.
Town counsel gave a wide cost range for a title search on the zero Shirley Reservoir parcel, and the committee's own funds were confirmed as separate from the general fund.

why_it_matters: A recommendation to hold back tax-lien sales is how land that has fallen into tax title can end up as town open space instead of going to a private buyer, so it touches what the town owns and what land stays undeveloped.
Title-search costs for the Shirley Reservoir parcel and the committee's own account show where open-space acquisition money would come from, which matters if a spending vote follows.
